title: My Bread Experiment
text: Three months ago, I decided to learn how to bake bread. I had never cooked anything difficult, so my first loaf was a disaster: it was flat, hard and almost impossible to cut. I nearly gave up, but my neighbour, who bakes every weekend, told me that most beginners use too much flour and too little patience. She showed me how to leave the dough in a warm place until it doubles in size. That small change made a huge difference. Now I bake twice a week, and my loaves are soft inside with a crisp outside. What I enjoy most isn't the eating, though. It's the quiet hour while the dough rises, when I have no phone, no emails and nothing to do except wait. Next, I'd like to try making bread with seeds and nuts.

title: Tool Library Opens in Eastbrook
text: A new "tool library" opened on Saturday in the town of Eastbrook, and by lunchtime more than a hundred people had visited. Instead of buying expensive equipment that they will use only once or twice, residents can borrow drills, ladders, garden tools and even sewing machines for a small yearly fee. The idea came from a retired builder, Hugo Marsh, who noticed that many garages in his street were full of unused tools. "People spend money on things that sit on a shelf," he said. "Sharing is cheaper, and it also brings neighbours together." Volunteers will teach short classes on basic repairs every Thursday evening. The organisers hope to add a repair café for broken electrical items by the end of the year. However, they are still looking for more volunteers to help with opening hours.

title: The Quiet Singer
text: Young Ben had a beautiful voice, but he only used it in the shower. When his music teacher told the school about a concert, she asked him to sing alone. His stomach turned over just thinking about it. For two weeks he practised in his room, and each night he promised himself that he would say no tomorrow. On the evening of the concert, he waited behind the curtain with his hands shaking. Then he noticed his little sister in the front row, holding a sign she had painted, which said "Go Ben!" in big letters. He breathed in deeply and stepped out. His first note was weak, but by the second line his voice was calm and strong. When he finished, the room was quiet for a second, and then everyone started to shout happily. Ben could not stop smiling.

title: Changing a Jacket
text:
Customer: Hello. I bought this jacket here last week, but it doesn't fit properly. The sleeves are too long.
Assistant: I'm sorry to hear that. Do you have your receipt?
Customer: Yes, here it is. I'd like to change it for a smaller size.
Assistant: Let me check. Oh, we don't have the same jacket in a smaller size at the moment, but we're getting more on Thursday.
Customer: I can't wait that long, because I need it for a trip on Wednesday.

Customer: I'll take the money, thanks. Actually, do you have any similar jackets in black?

title: The Forest at Dawn
text: Early in the morning, before the sun is fully up, the forest behind our house feels like a different world. The air is cool and slightly damp, and a white cloud sits low between the trees. At this hour the birds are at their loudest; their songs seem to come from every direction at once. If you stay very still, you may see a rabbit coming carefully out of the bushes, or a big bird flying home after the night. By nine o'clock, however, the cloud has gone, people have arrived with their dogs, and the animals have disappeared deeper into the trees. That is why I always set my alarm for five. For me, the best part of the forest is not what you see but the feeling of having it all to yourself.

title: Getting Ready for an Interview
text: A good interview begins long before you walk into the room. First, read the job advert carefully and make a list of the skills it asks for. Then think of one real example for each skill, for instance a time when you solved a problem or helped a team. Next, find out a little about the company; most firms have a website that explains what they do. Prepare two or three questions of your own, because this shows that you are interested. On the day, plan your journey so that you arrive about ten minutes early, not half an hour early, which can make the staff feel rushed. During the interview, listen to each question fully before you answer, and don't worry if you need a moment to think. Finally, send a short thank-you message the same day.
